title: AWS Bedrock (LLM)
description: Models on AWS Bedrock as an LLM tier, through gohort's Bedrock client, signed with an AWS credential that signs as this machine: its profile, SSO session or environment.
setup_notes: The credential signs as this machine's AWS identity, so set that up first: aws configure, or aws sso login for SSO, under the profile named here (blank uses $AWS_PROFILE, then the default chain). It needs bedrock:InvokeModel, and the model enabled in the region. To sign with an access key pair instead, edit the credential under API Credentials, switch off Sign as this machine and give ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET_ACCESS_KEY; a Bedrock API key goes in a bearer credential named in the spec's auth. The credential lands disabled: enable it under API Credentials. The connector lands unapproved: approve it in Admin > Extensions > Connectors and run Test on its row, which makes one short real chat. Then pick it under Admin > LLMs > Worker LLM (or Lead LLM) as Service: <name>. Choosing AWS Bedrock on the LLM form, or in first-run setup, installs this template for you. Converse speaks to any Bedrock model; InvokeModel to Claude only. Many accounts must call newer models through an inference profile: name the model as us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 rather than the bare id. Add per_million_input and per_million_output to the spec's cost to price its tokens.
